findings.title: Repeated warning turns forecast into feedback
findings.claim: The repeated warning presents the earlier saying as evidence about the learner's own response, while the denied capacity remains a practical ability conditioned by the learning relation.
findings.mechanism: The two q-w-l speech carriers in the focus repeat a prior statement; wider corrective-recall parallels at 68:28 and 2:33 make that return function as a feedback loop, while the t-w-ʿ capacity carrier links staying with the teacher to the learner's response.
findings.reader_payoff: The reminder can be perceived as tracking the learner's conduct, not only forecasting that the coming events will be difficult.
findings.containment: This deepens the plain rebuke that Moses cannot remain patient with the guide; it does not replace patience with another subject or make every warning a diagnostic device.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and the trusted cross-run record are explicit, but the represented reader-walk support and wider connection rows remain attributed interpretive evidence.
